AuditBrief.title: AuditBrief
AuditBrief.description:
Typed door-view of an ``seo_audit`` / ``cro_audit`` / ``marketing_scorecard`` brief.

All three audit blueprints scan a single URL, so they share this shape. Same contract
as ``ShowcaseBrief``: the persisted brief stays the free-form ``brief: dict`` (only
validated here at the door), and ``extra='allow'`` round-trips every other key.

intent.title: Intent
intent.description: Optional audience / goal to steer the enriched report prose

auditType.title: Audittype
auditType.description: Which scorecard family to run (marketing = the composite go-to-market scorecard)

includeLlm.title: Includellm
includeLlm.description: Produce the enriched (grounded, prose) report; false = deterministic titles only

AuditRequest.title: AuditRequest
AuditRequest.description: One-command audit input — a URL, optionally steered by an ``intent``.

AuditResponse.title: AuditResponse
AuditResponse.description:
The created project + deliverable + started run, with URLs to fetch the report
and stream live progress.

AuthoredSplit.title: AuthoredSplit
AuthoredSplit.description:
An author-pinned two-pane layout for one beat: this line's footage beside a
SECOND recorded clip (``h`` = left/right, ``v`` = top/bottom).

``second_clip`` is a footage-bearing line id / ``@clip-<n>`` tag — never a URL; the
compiler resolves it (``shared/footage_plans``). A pinned split bypasses the LLM
footage director for that line and wins over whatever the director or the critique
nudged.

BranchAncestor.title: BranchAncestor
BranchAncestor.description:
One hop of a branch's lineage on the way back to the ultimate root.

Since branch-of-branch is supported (a fork's link row points at whatever it forked,
so ``root`` is really the IMMEDIATE parent), a branch can sit several hops below the
root. ``is_branch`` distinguishes an intermediate parent (itself a branch) from the
ultimate root (a normal project) so the FE can render the chain and its terminal.

BranchContext.title: BranchContext
BranchContext.description:
Where-am-I context for a storyboard BRANCH project (migration 0052).

A branch is a real but HIDDEN project row (``projects.is_branch``); its linkage to
the root lives solely in ``storyboard_branches``. Without this block a user who
opens a branch has nothing telling them they are in one and no way back to the
root — a dead end. Populated on ``GET /api/projects/{id}`` for branch projects
only; ``null`` for every normal project.

``root_project_id`` / ``root_title`` name the IMMEDIATE parent (the merge target and
the back-navigation link); ``root_title`` is denormalised so the banner can render
"branch of <parent>" without a second round-trip. ``ancestors`` is the full lineage
from that immediate parent up to the ultimate root (``ancestors[0]`` == the immediate
parent, ``ancestors[-1]`` == the root; a single element for a direct branch), so the
banner can show the whole chain — "branch of B, which is a branch of A".

BranchCreateRequest.title: BranchCreateRequest
BranchCreateRequest.description: Body for opening a branch off a root project's current state.

BranchDiffResponse.title: BranchDiffResponse
BranchDiffResponse.description:
The diff, plus the optimistic-concurrency token the merge must hand back.

``root_fingerprint`` is a content hash of the ROOT's whole board (panels + scenes +
assets, normalised exactly as above). It is NOT a timestamp: a clock-based etag skews
across pods and a ``updated_at`` bump fires on writes that changed nothing. The merge
request echoes it; if the root moved in between, the merge is a 409 rather than a
silent clobber of whatever landed on main while the author was reading the diff.

Entries are BRANCH-CENTRIC: a panel that only main changed is not an entry (there is
nothing to merge). It still moves the fingerprint, which is the point.

BulkSlotResult.title: BulkSlotResult
BulkSlotResult.description:
A slot of the bulk write after it committed. ``change``: what happened;
``test``: the live test (``None`` when nothing was tested — unchanged/deleted).

ChapterTitleOverrides.title: ChapterTitleOverrides
ChapterTitleOverrides.description:
Operator edits to a course's chapter titles and sub-chapter visibility.

``overrides`` is keyed by each chapter's stable ``chapter_key`` (stable across
re-stitches, unlike sequence): the bare ``lesson_project_id`` for a per-lesson
(level-0) marker, ``f"{lesson_project_id}#{ordinal}"`` for a per-slide
(level-1) sub-chapter. Both levels are editable. Each title is trimmed and
must be 1-120 chars after trimming. The route 404s a key that no chapter
carries.

``hidden`` is the full set of level-1 ``chapter_key``\ s the operator wants
dropped from the published YouTube chapters and the in-app player (lesson
markers are the backbone and can never be hidden). It has full-replacement
semantics: ``None``/omitted leaves the stored hide set untouched (so a
title-only edit never wipes hides); ``[]`` clears all hides; a list sets the
hidden set to exactly those keys. The route 404s a key that is unknown or not
a level-1 sub-chapter.

ClipAudio.title: ClipAudio
ClipAudio.description:
Per-clip audio level on a Studio re-stitch. Applies to the shot's PRIMARY
audio (narration/clip audio_url) only — NOT the music bed (see MusicEdit).
All-defaults is a no-op the compiler omits (byte-identical).

ClipEdit.title: ClipEdit
ClipEdit.description:
Per-clip edit overrides merged onto a spine element before re-stitch.

Every field is optional; only fields the client actually sends are patched
(the route uses ``model_dump(exclude_unset=True)``), so omitting a field
leaves that clip's current value untouched. Sending a field as ``null``
explicitly CLEARS a previously-authored override back to the computed default
— the override ladder's "unset" step.

- ``clip_lead_seconds`` — seconds of recorded footage to skip at the head
  (drop the app's blank load-in). Only meaningful for a footage clip; a no-op
  on an image/text-card shot (``assemble_shots._attach_clip_framing``).
- ``clip_out_seconds`` — the source-timeline OUT-point (seconds from the head
  of the recording) closing the window ``clip_lead_seconds`` opened:
  ``clip_lead_seconds=4.0`` + ``clip_out_seconds=7.5`` shows exactly 4.0s-7.5s
  of the source, which is the only way to cut SEVERAL shots out of ONE long
  recording. Measured on the SOURCE timeline, so it is independent of
  ``speed``. Unlike ``clip_lead_seconds`` (start-anchor only), the compiler
  honours it under BOTH anchors. Must be strictly greater than
  ``clip_lead_seconds`` — the compiler declares ``exclusiveMinimum: 0`` and
  rejects a non-increasing window, so we reject it here as a 422 rather than
  pay for a failed compile.
- ``clip_anchor`` — ``start`` shows the head (after any lead), ``end`` shows
  the settled tail of the recording. ``auto`` defers to build_shots, which
  resolves the motion-settled hero-frame lead from the clip's
  ``motion_timeline`` (emitting ``start`` + a numeric lead), degrading to the
  default framing when the curve cannot localise a moment.
- ``caption`` — burned-in caption text for this clip; wins over the computed
  caption and emits even when the deliverable's captions are off. Empty
  string or ``null`` clears the override back to the computed default.
- ``fit`` — how the clip's visual fills the frame (``contain`` = letterbox,
  ``cover`` = crop-fill, ``scroll`` = pan a tall capture).
- ``speed`` — playback rate multiplier (``1.0`` = real time, ``2.0`` = 2x fast,
  ``0.5`` = half-speed slow-mo). Orthogonal to the narration-duration reconcile:
  the compositor retimes the visual, it does not shorten the shot's ``seconds``.
- ``transition`` — the mix/wipe cut ENTERING this clip; ``null`` restores the
  default hard cut.
- ``adjust`` — a per-clip colour grade (brightness / contrast / saturation /
  gamma + optional look preset); ``null`` restores the ungraded source.
- ``overlays`` — burned-in text titles/lower-thirds layered over this clip;
  ``null`` or an empty list clears any authored overlays.
- ``audio`` — a per-clip audio-level edit (gain / mute / fade-in / fade-out)
  on the shot's PRIMARY audio (narration / clip audio); ``null`` restores the
  unmodified audio.
- ``audio_url`` — an uploaded voiceover (``POST /api/uploads/voiceover``) that
  REPLACES this shot's TTS narration; ``null`` clears it back to TTS. Strictly
  orthogonal to ``audio``: ``audio`` LEVELS whatever the primary audio is,
  ``audio_url`` changes what the primary audio *is* — both may be set and they
  compose.
- ``audio_seconds`` — the server-probed duration of that upload. It DECLARES
  this shot's length (the compiler ffprobes the audio and freeze-pads the
  visual to it), so it must ride along with ``audio_url``; the upload route is
  the only thing that sets it (never hand-authored).

ClipTransition.title: ClipTransition
ClipTransition.description:
The cut ENTERING a clip, applied on a Studio re-stitch.

Mirrors the compositor's ``Shot.transition``: ``type`` is the mix/wipe family
and ``duration`` is the crossfade length in seconds. It rides the spine element
like the other per-clip edits (``patch_elements_in_output``) and reaches the
compositor unchanged as a ``{type, duration}`` dict. Describes the incoming cut,
so the first shot's transition is a no-op (there is no cut before it).

ColorAdjust.title: ColorAdjust
ColorAdjust.description:
Per-clip colour grade applied on a Studio re-stitch.

Mirrors the compiler's per-clip colour contract: ``brightness`` shifts
exposure, ``contrast`` / ``saturation`` / ``gamma`` are multiplicative dials
(``1.0`` = identity), and an optional ``preset`` names a canned look the
compiler expands into the same param space. It rides the spine element like
the other per-clip edits (``patch_elements_in_output``) and reaches the
compiler unchanged as an ``{brightness, contrast, saturation, gamma, preset}``
dict. All-defaults (or ``null`` on the ``ClipEdit`` field) is an identity
grade the compiler omits.

ConnectionDraft.title: ConnectionDraft
ConnectionDraft.description:
A connection configuration to test or store.

``secret``: absent (or ``null``) = keep the stored secret, ``""`` = clear it,
any other value = set it. Keeping is refused when ``kind`` or the endpoint
changes (the stored key was entrusted to one endpoint).

ConnectionPut.title: ConnectionPut
ConnectionPut.description:
``PUT`` body: a draft plus the optimistic-concurrency guard.

``expected_version`` is the version the client last saw (``0`` = no tenant
connection yet); a mismatch is 409.

ConnectionTestResult.title: ConnectionTestResult
ConnectionTestResult.description:
``ok`` is ``None`` when the kind has no auth-only endpoint (``probed=False``):
nothing was sent, so neither a pass nor a failure is claimed.

ConnectionView.title: ConnectionView
ConnectionView.description: The tenant's current connection on a slot. Never the secret.

ConnectionsBulkPut.title: ConnectionsBulkPut
ConnectionsBulkPut.description:
The whole tenant subtree in one write.

``connections``: slot → ``ConnectionPut`` (set) or ``null`` (delete → back to the
deployment default). Slots not named are left untouched. ``dependencies``: w2v has
no configurable dependency (webscraper / media-discovery are fixed), so anything non-empty is 422.

CritiqueAuthInfo.title: CritiqueAuthInfo
CritiqueAuthInfo.description:
Mirror of analysis_service ``AuthInfo``: credentials analysis applies when
fetching the target URL (basic / bearer / cookie replay). Same field rules.

CritiqueCreate.title: CritiqueCreate
CritiqueCreate.description:
Inbound body for starting a critique — mirrors analysis_service's
``CritiqueRequest`` (``src/domains/critique/schemas.py``) field-for-field,
including its "exactly one content source" rule, so a body analysis would
accept is accepted here and one it would reject is a 422 here (not a
proxied 422 after a hop).

Content source — exactly one of:

* ``url``          crawl a live page (the w2v frontend's path);
* ``html``         score pre-rendered HTML in place (merqi marketing's
                   branding-render critique + copy diagnostics, P9-7);
* ``artifact_ref`` an object key in analysis's own bucket, tenant-confined
                   server-side by analysis.

Size: ``ProxyBodyLimitMiddleware`` caps this exact route at analysis's own
``MAX_HTML_SIZE`` (10 MiB) + a 64 KiB JSON envelope — a body analysis would
score is never refused here, a larger one is a 413 (declared or streamed),
and the cap is a streaming count, so nothing is buffered before Auth.

Deliberately NOT exposed (analysis accepts them; a public API-key caller
must not): ``llm_config`` — its ``base_url`` + ``api_key_env`` would let a
caller point analysis's LLM call at their own host carrying any env-named
secret of analysis; ``site_analysis`` — orchestrator-computed context that
steers which security checks run. ``extra="forbid"`` makes sending either
(or any unknown field) a loud 422 instead of a silent drop.

CritiqueFindingInput.title: CritiqueFindingInput
CritiqueFindingInput.description:
A critique finding used to weight proposal severity — mirror of the FE
``CritiqueFinding`` (only the fields the model reads are required).

DeploymentDefaults.title: DeploymentDefaults
DeploymentDefaults.description: What applies where the tenant leaves a field ``null`` (read-only).

DiffEntry.title: DiffEntry
DiffEntry.description:
One panel's three-way story, keyed by LINEAGE — never by panel id.

``key`` is the panel's ``origin_id`` if it has one, else its own id. Every side
resolves to the same key: a root panel is its own origin, and the fork stamped that
id onto the child's copy. Panel ids are re-minted per project, so keying on them
would make every panel look "added" on one side and "deleted" on the other.

``base`` / ``main`` / ``branch`` are the normalised panel payloads of the three
sides (``None`` where the panel does not exist on that side), so the UI can render
three columns without re-fetching. They are NORMALISED, not raw rows: ``scene`` and
the ``characters`` / ``props`` / ``location`` roles are expressed as LINEAGE keys,
because the raw ids differ per project and would otherwise report a spurious edit on
every forked panel.

Approval state (``status`` / ``approved_at`` / ``approved_by``) is deliberately NOT
part of the compared surface: approval is the ROOT's governance record. Diffing it
would let a merge forge an approval on the root (a branch author approving their own
copy) or silently unapprove a root panel — neither has a corresponding root-side
trail event. Merge carries CONTENT; approvals stay where they were granted.

EnhancePromptResponse.title: EnhancePromptResponse
EnhancePromptResponse.description: The rewritten prompt. Never the original — the caller already has it.

FeatureSuggestionInput.title: FeatureSuggestionInput
FeatureSuggestionInput.description: A single fix/feature proposal — mirror of the FE ``FeatureSuggestion``.

FromIntentRequest.title: FromIntentRequest
FromIntentRequest.description:
The A0 authoring-front-door request (great-video PR 2.2): a declarative
``VideoIntent`` + one deliverable's packaging knobs. The orchestrator resolves the
intent into a computed plan (``resolve_plan``) at run-start and drives the existing
DAG — the author supplies ~15 lines of intent instead of a hand-tuned brief.

FromIntentResponse.title: FromIntentResponse
FromIntentResponse.description:
The created project + deliverable + started run, with URLs to inspect the
computed plan (``config_snapshot['plan_document']``) and stream live progress.

IntakeBody.title: IntakeBody
IntakeBody.description:
What early-access-intake forwards (``forwarded_body``): requester-typed
text is normalised to one printable line (``message`` keeps newlines).

InviteCreated.title: InviteCreated
InviteCreated.description:
The invite + its one-time link. The token is shown ONLY here (create and
resend); the database keeps its SHA-256.

KindField.title: KindField
KindField.description:
One form input. ``key``: ``base_url`` | ``model`` | ``options.<name>``.
``required`` is the server's rule (a PUT without it is 422), not a hint.

KindRequirements.title: KindRequirements
KindRequirements.description: Fields a connection of one tenant kind must carry (drives the Providers form).

LegacyIdentityBody.title: LegacyIdentityBody
LegacyIdentityBody.description:
The login a LEGACY row (approved before logins were stamped) created:
its Keycloak user id and the operator's evidence (kept as a fingerprint only).

LegalBrief.title: LegalBrief
LegalBrief.description:
Typed door-view of ``brief.legal`` — the ``claim_finish`` (A18) opt-in gate.

``claim_finish`` wakes ONLY on an explicit ``legal.mode`` of ``auto`` or
``critique_only`` (``stages/demo_video/claim_finish.py`` ``_ACTIVE_MODES``);
anything else silently skips the stage for the whole run. Until now ``mode`` was
validated NOWHERE, so an operator who typed ``"critique-only"`` (hyphen) or
``"Auto"`` got a 201 at the door and a legal gate that never ran — discoverable
only by reading stage rows after the fact. A present-but-invalid ``mode`` now
422s here instead.

⚠️ ``mode`` is OPTIONAL and the model is ``extra='allow'``, deliberately. The
``legal`` block ALREADY ships in prod carrying
``{"trademarks": [...], "defensibility": "..."}`` for other consumers and NO
``mode`` key; that shape must keep validating (and must keep leaving claim_finish
inert — the existing, intended opt-in behaviour). Only an explicitly-supplied bad
``mode`` is rejected.

``mode`` is the ONLY typed field, also deliberately. ``posture`` and the
``claims`` sub-block (``allow_superlatives`` / ``on_unsupported`` / ``iterations``
/ ``score_threshold``) ride on ``extra='allow'`` untyped: ``claim_finish`` itself
defends with ``if not isinstance(claims_cfg, dict): claims_cfg = {}``, which is
direct evidence that a NON-dict ``legal.claims`` (e.g. a list of claim strings in
a legal/trademark block) is anticipated in the wild. Typing that sub-block would
422 such a brief at create — a regression on payloads that are valid today. The
stage already defaults every claims knob, so a bad one degrades to a default; a
bad ``mode`` silently disables the whole stage. Only the latter is worth a 422.

LicenseStatus.title: LicenseStatus
LicenseStatus.description:
Rich, app-scoped license status for the SPA (GET /api/license/status).

``state ∈ active|expiring_soon|expired|revoked|none|unknown``. Fail-soft:
``unknown`` means an upstream lookup blip, not a block. Mirrors fr's
``/api/license/status`` contract so the frontend gate ports directly.

LlmAccessView.title: LlmAccessView
LlmAccessView.description: The tenant's LLM access posture (licences ``byo_mode`` for app ``w2v``).

MediaRef.title: MediaRef
MediaRef.description:
Where a panel's picture lives — serialized into the JSONB ``media_ref`` blob.
All optional so a text-only (Phase-0) panel persists with an empty ``{}``.

MergeRequest.title: MergeRequest
MergeRequest.description:
``root_fingerprint`` is REQUIRED — it is the whole concurrency contract.

``resolutions`` need only cover what the caller wants to override: a non-conflict
entry defaults to ``branch`` (the author asked to merge their branch). A ``conflict``
entry has NO default — merging one unresolved is a 422, because guessing which side
wins is precisely the decision the human opened the diff to make.

MergeResolution.title: MergeResolution
MergeResolution.description:
Per-entry verdict. ``branch`` applies the branch side onto the root; ``main``
keeps the root's version; ``skip`` leaves the panel alone (identical effect to
``main`` — both are a no-op write — but they say different things in the audit and
the UI, so the vocabulary keeps them apart). ``keep_both`` (conflicts only) keeps the
root's version AND brings the branch's conflicting panel across as a NEW panel with a
fresh, non-colliding ``shot_key`` — the "I want both cuts" resolution.

ModelsRequest.title: ModelsRequest
ModelsRequest.description:
``POST /{slot}/models`` body. ``secret`` absent/``null`` = use the stored
secret (only while kind and base URL are unchanged).

MusicEdit.title: MusicEdit
MusicEdit.description:
Run-level music-bed override applied on a Studio re-stitch.

``track`` is a sound-catalog **music** id (e.g. the built-ins ``corporate_uplift``
/ ``ambient_tech`` / ``jazz_lounge``); ``null`` or ``""`` turns the music bed
OFF (other sound design — transitions / ambient — is untouched). The remaining
fields tune the bed; each omitted field keeps the run's current value. Applied
by merging into the parent run's ``sound_effects`` config and re-stitching, so a
per-run override never mutates the project brief. An unknown ``track`` (not a
music id in ``GET /api/music/tracks`` for the caller's tenant — e.g. the track's
human LABEL instead of its id) is rejected with 422 by ``apply-edits``.

``action_reel`` (and any pipeline that times its cut to the bed) handles the
same payload differently, because it must: the child run re-runs from
``music_select`` so the new track's beat grid is fetched and the cut re-snapped
to it, and the override rides the ``music`` config block rather than
``sound_effects`` — merged onto the parent's block, so the keeps-the-current-value
rule above holds on that product too. On that product ``duck_db`` cannot be applied at all and is
reported as an ignored field in the run's notes; a falsy ``track`` renders a
SILENT, evenly-spaced reel and is likewise noted (the run reads ``degraded``).

MusicTrack.title: MusicTrack
MusicTrack.description:
One selectable music bed (a ``music``-category asset in the catalog).

``id`` is the catalog id a run's config block references; ``label`` is the
human/UI-readable description; ``category`` is always ``"music"`` here.

MusicTracksResponse.title: MusicTracksResponse
MusicTracksResponse.description: The music beds available to the caller's tenant (built-in + manifests).

OffboardingApprove.title: OffboardingApprove
OffboardingApprove.description:
Approve = execute. A delete needs the plan's ``confirm_token``; ``force``
overrides the overridable blockers (missing export, live/unverified licence,
partner tenant) and is audited.

OffboardingPlan.title: OffboardingPlan
OffboardingPlan.description:
Step 1 of the two-step delete: what a delete would do, and the token step 2
(``DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id}?confirm=<token>``) must echo.

OffboardingRequestCreate.title: OffboardingRequestCreate
OffboardingRequestCreate.description: A tenant_admin's request; a super_admin decides and executes it.

PackagingIntent.title: PackagingIntent
PackagingIntent.description:
Authoring hints for the deliverable's packaging (title / description /
thumbnail). ``extra='allow'`` — forward-compat for packaging knobs not yet
typed here.

PanelApproveRequest.title: PanelApproveRequest
PanelApproveRequest.description: Body for approve/unapprove — an optional free-text note recorded on the event.

PanelGen.title: PanelGen
PanelGen.description:
Generation provenance for a panel's picture — serialized into the JSONB
``gen`` blob alongside :class:`MediaRef`.

``seed`` is the reproducibility contract: the image runner is text→image plus
a seed (no img2img, no ControlNet, no IP-Adapter), so the prompt and the seed
together are the ONLY things that can reproduce the picture or keep a
character on-model across panels. ``media_id`` is the content-addressed id
the artifact store keyed the object under, so a regenerate with identical
inputs can find it instead of paying for a second generation.

``size`` is the image's MEASURED ``"{width}x{height}"``, read off the
delivered bytes — not the size that was requested. The two differ: the
generator overrides the request (a 1024x1024 ask came back 1536x1536 in
prod), and recording the ask made this field state something the picture
beside it contradicted. It is ``None`` whenever the bytes never passed
through this service (a reused stored object, or a provider CDN url served
straight through) or carried no readable PNG header — unknown, not guessed.

PanelImageJobResponse.title: PanelImageJobResponse
PanelImageJobResponse.description:
Status of one panel-image generation.

``queued``/``running`` are transient; ``completed`` carries the panel's new
``media_ref`` + ``gen`` (so a client that polls need not re-fetch the panel),
``failed`` carries ``error``. The durable record is the PANEL, not this — the
job is TTL-bounded progress metadata.

A generated ``media_ref.url`` is served as the panel's image-proxy path
(``/api/storyboard/panels/{id}/image/content``) rather than the stored
``minio.internal`` URL, which no browser outside the cluster can resolve; a url
the proxy cannot serve (an external image) is passed through untouched. The
path addresses the PANEL's current image rather than this job's snapshot of
it, so a client that caches an image url is caching a pointer to the durable
record — which is the panel, not this.

PanelImageRequest.title: PanelImageRequest
PanelImageRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/storyboard/panels/{id}/image``.

Everything is optional: the prompt is composed server-side from the panel's
own direction plus its referenced assets' canonical descriptors, and the
seed is taken from the referenced assets so a character stays on-model
across the board. Overrides exist for the operator who wants a different
aspect, provider, or an explicit re-roll.

There is deliberately NO reference-image field. The image runner is
text→image plus a seed; it cannot be conditioned on a picture, so accepting
one here would be a lie in the API surface.

PartnerApiKeyCreate.title: PartnerApiKeyCreate
PartnerApiKeyCreate.description:
``POST /api/tenants/{tenant_id}/api-keys`` — a partner mints a machine key
for a tenant bound to its partner licence. ``name`` is the idempotency key
(a second mint of a LIVE name is 409 ``API_KEY_NAME_EXISTS``).

PartnerTenantCreate.title: PartnerTenantCreate
PartnerTenantCreate.description:
``tenant_id`` makes the call idempotent (omit → a new id is minted).

``admin_email`` is OPTIONAL (P9-4): absent → no first-admin invite; the
tenant is managed by the partner's machine keys (a super_admin can still
invite a human later).

PendingInvite.title: PendingInvite
PendingInvite.description:
A pending, unexpired invite addressed to the caller's VERIFIED email
(``AuthMe.pending_invites``). Listing it accepts nothing — the caller joins
explicitly via ``POST /api/invites/{id}/accept``. Deliberately minimal: no
inviter, no email, no token.

PlatformChannelIn.title: PlatformChannelIn
PlatformChannelIn.description: The platform fallback channel. Absent/``null`` secrets = keep the stored ones.

PlatformDependency.title: PlatformDependency

ProjectDraftCreate.title: ProjectDraftCreate
ProjectDraftCreate.description:
Minimal create-door for the wizard's EARLY draft: a real project row with a
chosen ``type`` but NO deliverables yet.

Deliberately kept separate from (and does NOT relax) the strict ``ProjectCreate``
used by the normal final-submit / n8n path — that one still requires >=1
deliverable + runs the typed-brief door. A draft has no brief/deliverables yet;
the wizard adds them + PATCHes + starts runs via the existing endpoints later.

``type`` stays REQUIRED so the DB CHECK still enforces a valid project type (an
unknown value 422s at the Literal door before it ever reaches the DB) — no
migration or schema change is needed. ``status`` server-defaults to ``drafting``;
zero deliverables is legal (deliverables are a child table).

RedesignCreate.title: RedesignCreate
RedesignCreate.description:
Inbound body for starting a redesign. Mirrors the fields of
analysis_service's ``RedesignRequest`` that the standalone tool exposes.

RegenerateClip.title: RegenerateClip
RegenerateClip.description:
Regenerate a single clip's image and re-stitch the video.

``stage_name`` is the run's clip-spine stage; ``element_id`` is the clip's
spine element id (``shot.id`` / ``line.id``) that open feedback is pinned to.
The route spawns a child run that preserves the spine verbatim (siblings
untouched) and re-runs only the per-clip image stage onward, folding the
clip's feedback into just that clip's prompt so exactly one image
regenerates. Falls back to annotation-driven regenerate when the pipeline has
no per-clip image stage (422).

RegenerateRequest.title: RegenerateRequest
RegenerateRequest.description:
Create a child run that re-runs part of the pipeline.

``from_stage`` (optional) targets a specific stage: re-run it and everything
depending on it, reuse every other completed stage — the "rerun this stage"
action. When omitted, the per-stage restart plan decides (see
``GET /runs/{id}/restart-plan``): unfinished, fed-back, input-changed and
edit-dependent stages re-run, the rest is reused. 422 if ``from_stage`` is not a
stage of this run's blueprint.

Renarrate.title: Renarrate
Renarrate.description:
Re-narrate a single line: new narration text and/or a new voice.

``stage_name`` is the run's clip-spine stage; ``element_id`` is the clip's
spine element id. An omitted ``narration_text`` keeps the line's current text;
an omitted ``voice`` uses the run's configured voice. At least one must be
given (otherwise the request is a no-op that would still burn a TTS call).

The route spawns a child run that re-synthesizes EXACTLY ONE clip and re-runs
only the compile stage — every sibling clip's audio is reused verbatim. 422 if
the clip already carries an uploaded voiceover (which would win over the TTS).

ReorderClips.title: ReorderClips
ReorderClips.description:
Rearrange the clip timeline and re-stitch the video.

``stage_name`` is the run's clip-spine stage (the storyboard / gen stage whose
output holds the ordered clip array). ``ordered_element_ids`` is the full set
of that stage's element ids in the desired new order — a permutation of the
current ids (missing, extra, or duplicate ids → 400). The route spawns a
child run that preserves every upstream stage (spine reordered) and re-runs
only the compile stage onward, reusing all generated clip assets.

ReorderPanels.title: ReorderPanels
ReorderPanels.description: Permutation of the project's panel row-ids (mirror ``ReorderChildren``).

ReorderScenes.title: ReorderScenes
ReorderScenes.description: Permutation of the project's scene row-ids (mirror ``ReorderPanels``).

RestartPlanReason.title: RestartPlanReason

RestartPlanResponse.title: RestartPlanResponse
RestartPlanResponse.description:
What ``POST /runs/{id}/regenerate {}`` would reuse and re-run, right now.

``mode="partial"`` reuses every ``reuse`` stage; ``mode="full"`` re-runs every
stage and ``full_reasons`` says why. ``changed_inputs`` lists the run inputs that
differ from the ones the run was started with (``live:<x>`` = project data a
stage reads live, e.g. uploaded footage). ``stages`` is in pipeline order.

RestartPlanStage.title: RestartPlanStage
RestartPlanStage.description: One stage of a restart plan: reused as-is, or re-run — and why.

RestoreSnapshotRequest.title: RestoreSnapshotRequest
RestoreSnapshotRequest.description:
Body for a snapshot restore — the whole-board optimistic-concurrency map.

Restore rewrites scenes + panels + assets wholesale, so the caller must state the board
state it is restoring OVER: one flat ``{row id: lock_version}`` map covering every live
scene, panel and asset (uuid7 ids share one namespace, so no bucketing). Anything added,
deleted or edited since that read → 409, instead of silently discarding it.

ReviewInbox.title: ReviewInbox
ReviewInbox.description: The caller's review notices, oldest wait first (the count is ``len(items)``).

ReviewInboxItem.title: ReviewInboxItem
ReviewInboxItem.description: One run the caller owns that is paused at a review checkpoint.

input_tokens.title: Input Tokens
input_tokens.description: Sum of input (prompt) tokens across the run's usage rows.

output_tokens.title: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Sum of output (completion) tokens across the run's usage rows.

RunStart.title: RunStart
RunStart.description:
Body for ``POST /api/deliverables/{id}/runs``.

``pause_after_stages`` semantics:

* ``None`` (field omitted) → seed from the blueprint's
  ``default_pause_after`` stage specs (so e.g. promo runs pause after
  script + storyboard for creative review by default, matching the
  blueprint declaration). This is the SPA default — ``runs.start()``
  without args sends an empty body.
* ``[]`` (explicit empty list) → autopilot, no checkpoints.
* ``[stage_name, ...]`` → user-chosen checkpoint set.

The empty-default sentinel changed in 2026-05-31: previously the
field defaulted to ``[]`` which silently turned every run into
autopilot, contradicting the blueprint's declared pause defaults
and the run-monitor UI's intent to pause for the user to review.

RunStatusLite.title: RunStatusLite
RunStatusLite.description:
Lightweight run status for the live-monitor poll.

Field names mirror the subset of ``RunDetail`` that the frontend
``StateReconciler`` reads (``status``/``current_stage``/``error`` +
``stage_outputs`` statuses), so the client reconciler is unchanged — only
the wire payload shrinks. Omits ``config_snapshot``, ``usage_total`` and
every stage ``output`` blob.

input_tokens.title: Input Tokens
input_tokens.description: Sum of input (prompt) tokens across the run's usage rows.

output_tokens.title: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Sum of output (completion) tokens across the run's usage rows.

RunUsageReport.title: RunUsageReport
RunUsageReport.description:
``POST /api/runs/{run_id}/usage`` — one LLM call a downstream service made on
the platform vLLM for this run. Snake-case wire names, no aliases: this is an S2S
contract (w2v_common's reporter), not an SPA payload.

RunUsageReportResult.title: RunUsageReportResult
RunUsageReportResult.description: ``recorded=False`` ⇒ this ``call_id`` was already recorded for the run.

cost_settled.title: Cost Settled
cost_settled.description: True once the cost is final (terminal run, billing mirror reconciled). While False, cost_usd is partial or not yet known.

RunUsageTotal.title: RunUsageTotal
RunUsageTotal.description:
A run's usage + cost.

``cost_status="unavailable"`` means the cost could not be priced (e.g.
``cost_unavailable_reason="billing_credential_missing"``) — ``cost_usd`` is
then ``None``, never ``0``: an unknown cost must not be renderable as $0. The
validator makes the two states mutually exclusive by construction.
``by_stage`` still lists the rows that ARE known locally.

ScopeSwitchAuditRequest.title: ScopeSwitchAuditRequest
ScopeSwitchAuditRequest.description:
Record a deliberate super-admin scope switch. ``to_tenant_id`` None = the
super-admin reset back to their own tenant (action ``scope.reset``).

ServiceErrorView.title: ServiceErrorView
ServiceErrorView.description: The refusal a failed run recorded, in the same code the HTTP edge returns.

ServiceProviderView.title: ServiceProviderView
ServiceProviderView.description: Where a run's output came from: ``deployment`` or ``tenant`` provider.

ServiceRunView.title: ServiceRunView
ServiceRunView.description: One persisted service-lab run. ``media_url`` is a path on THIS service (``/api/services/{slot}/history/{id}/media``) rather than a MinIO URL: the object is in the orchestrator's own bucket and is only reachable with its credentials, so the browser gets a proxied path it can put straight into ```` / ``

SetPrivacyRequest.title: SetPrivacyRequest
SetPrivacyRequest.description: Body of the governed release: the visibility to raise a private upload to.

ShowcaseBrief.title: ShowcaseBrief
ShowcaseBrief.description:
Typed view of a showcase project's brief.

Documents + validates the keys the showcase blueprint reads; the persisted shape
stays the free-form ``brief: dict`` (same contract as ``ProjectResponse.source_url``).
``extra='allow'`` keeps the many other brief keys (title_card / ken_burns / dialogue /
sound_effects / …) round-tripping untouched — only the typed fields are validated.

ShowcaseLine.title: ShowcaseLine
ShowcaseLine.description:
API request contract for one authored clip↔beat: narration bound to a recorded
``@clip-<n>`` footage tag.

Shares the ``AuthoredLine`` field set (single source of truth in
``src.models.showcase_line``) with the demo_video stage-output twin
``services/stages/demo_video/gen.py::DemoVideoLine`` — so the two can no longer
drift. This variant adds the request-door strictness the pipeline relies on
(non-empty narration, ``clip_anchor`` admits ``'end'`` plus ``'auto'``) plus the
``_camel`` config; the stage twin stays permissive.

``clip_anchor="auto"`` is a content-aware request — build_shots resolves it to
the motion-settled hero-frame lead (``clip_anchor="start"`` + numeric
``clip_lead_seconds``) from the clip's ``motion_timeline`` at compile time; an
unresolvable curve degrades to the default framing.

SiblingMergeRequest.title: SiblingMergeRequest
SiblingMergeRequest.description:
Merge one branch INTO a SIBLING — both forked off the same parent, so the parent's
shared ``branch_base`` is their common ancestor for a symmetric three-way.

``target_branch_id`` is the sibling to merge into; ``target_fingerprint`` (from the
sibling diff) is the concurrency contract on the TARGET board — a 409 if it moved.
``resolutions`` follow the same rules as a branch->root merge (a conflict has no default).

SiblingMergeResponse.title: SiblingMergeResponse
SiblingMergeResponse.description:
Both branches stay OPEN — a sibling merge cross-pollinates, it does not close a
lifecycle: the source is not ``merged`` (its content never reached the root) and neither
child is archived. Only the TARGET board changed; ``target_fingerprint`` is its post-merge
hash, so a chained sibling merge can proceed without re-reading the diff.

SlotRequirement.title: SlotRequirement

SlotUsage.title: SlotUsage
SlotUsage.description:
A blueprint stage that may call the slot. ``when``: ``always`` (whenever the
stage runs) or the brief opt-in without which the stage skips.

SlotView.title: SlotView
SlotView.description:
One registry slot as the Providers page shows it.

``type``: ``connection`` = stored here (``writable`` says whether a tenant may);
``grant`` = connected through its own flow (``publish.youtube`` → the YouTube
OAuth grant), never written through this API and never pinned per run.

SnapshotCreateRequest.title: SnapshotCreateRequest
SnapshotCreateRequest.description: Body for a manual snapshot — an optional free-text note.

StageElementPatch.title: StageElementPatch
StageElementPatch.description:
Shallow-merge patch payload for one element inside a stage's JSONB output.

Keys present here override the matching keys on the element; nested keys
are NOT recursed into (last-write-wins on the whole nested value). The
element's `id` field is preserved regardless of what's in `patch`.

StageElementRestamp.title: StageElementRestamp
StageElementRestamp.description:
Full-replacement payload for one element + dirty-mark downstream stages.

Unlike `StageElementPatch` (shallow-merge in place, no downstream effect),
a restamp replaces the addressed element with `value` and resets every
downstream stage_output of the same run to `status='pending'` with
`output=null`. After a restamp, a subsequent `POST /runs/{id}/regenerate`
re-executes from the first dirty stage.

The element's `id` is preserved regardless of `value` content.

StageStatusLite.title: StageStatusLite
StageStatusLite.description:
Per-stage status without the (potentially multi-MB) ``output`` blob.

The run-monitor's safety-net poll only needs each stage's lifecycle state;
shipping the full ``StageOutputResponse.output`` JSONB every poll tick
grew the payload with each completed stage and saturated the browser main
thread on long runs. This is the trimmed shape it polls instead.

StoryboardAssetImageUploadResponse.title: StoryboardAssetImageUploadResponse
StoryboardAssetImageUploadResponse.description:
The URL an operator drops onto ``StoryboardAsset.reference_images``.

``width``/``height`` are best-effort pixel dimensions read from the image
HEADER (no full decode). They are ``None`` when the header is unreadable —
the upload is never failed on a dimension read, because the bytes have
already passed the magic-byte gate and the field is advisory (the FE uses it
to lay the thumbnail out).

TTSPreviewRequest.title: TTSPreviewRequest
TTSPreviewRequest.description:
Inbound body for a voice preview. All fields optional — the TTS service
applies its own provider/voice defaults when omitted.

TenantLicenceTokenResult.title: TenantLicenceTokenResult
TenantLicenceTokenResult.description: Never carries the token — only what it resolved to.

TenantLicenceTokenSet.title: TenantLicenceTokenSet
TenantLicenceTokenSet.description:
``PUT /api/tenants/{tenant_id}/licence-token`` — rotate / hand over the
tenant's stored licence token (the owning partner, or super_admin).

TenantOAuthClientIn.title: TenantOAuthClientIn
TenantOAuthClientIn.description: A tenant's own Google OAuth client. Both fields required (upstream contract).

TenantPartnerBind.title: TenantPartnerBind
TenantPartnerBind.description:
``PUT /api/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/partner`` — bind an EXISTING tenant to
an allow-listed partner licence so that partner can mint its keys. Unknown
fields are refused: the retired ``licence_id`` must not be silently ignored.

TextOverlay.title: TextOverlay
TextOverlay.description:
A burned-in text title/lower-third layered over a clip on re-stitch.

Mirrors the compiler's per-clip overlay contract: ``text`` is the string to
draw, ``position`` picks a nine-grid anchor (an explicit ``x`` / ``y`` pixel
pair overrides the anchor when both are set), ``font_size`` / ``color`` style
it, and ``start`` / ``end`` window it in seconds (absent = the whole clip). A
clip carries a list of these; the compiler draws them in order over the
graded frame.

ThumbnailOverride.title: ThumbnailOverride
ThumbnailOverride.description:
Operator override for a course's video thumbnail / poster.

``thumbnail_url`` is an artifact URL the orchestrator can presign (a MinIO
object it owns or a local ``file://`` artifact — validated route-side).
``None`` clears the override and reverts to the auto AI cover.

VerbatimItemListResponse.title: VerbatimItemListResponse
VerbatimItemListResponse.description: List envelope the SPA's verbatim store expects (``{items, total}``).

VerbatimItemResponse.title: VerbatimItemResponse
VerbatimItemResponse.description:
SPA-facing verbatim row.

None of these lifecycle/identity fields is stored on ``verbatim_items``
(0009 created them, the v3 reset 0015 dropped the table CASCADE, 0017
re-added only kind/hint/scope/scope_target). They resolve as follows:

* ``tenant_id`` / ``subject_id`` / ``visibility`` — INHERITED from the
  parent Project by the route's ``_resp``.
* ``status`` / ``placed_in_stage`` / ``placed_in_element_id`` — DERIVED at
  read time by ``src.services.verbatim_placement.derive_placements``, which
  re-matches the phrase against a run's currently-persisted carrier stage
  outputs. Derivation only happens on ``verbatim.list`` when the caller
  passes ``?run_id=`` (placement is a property of a RUN, not of the row);
  every other response — and a list with no ``run_id`` — correctly keeps the
  ``pending`` default, because without a run there is nothing to match
  against. All three ``VerbatimStatus`` values are reachable: ``placed``,
  ``pending`` ("an eligible stage ran and the phrase is not in it, or nothing
  has run yet") and ``rejected`` ("every stage that ran was forbidden from
  carrying this item's ``kind``" — today that is every ``slide`` item, since
  every stage in ``STAGE_VERBATIM_KIND`` consumes ``tts``).
* ``retry_count`` — genuinely unimplemented; always 0.

v3 dropped per-job verbatim, so job_id is always null. See migration 0017
for the live column shape.

VideoAnalyzeCreate.title: VideoAnalyzeCreate
VideoAnalyzeCreate.description:
What recon sends. Deliberately ONLY ``video_url``: video-analyzer's other
request fields (pipeline/verification config) are not a public surface.

VideoIntent.title: VideoIntent
VideoIntent.description:
The declarative authoring front door: one ergonomic contract describing the
video an author wants. Standalone — deliberately NOT registered in any
per-type create-door model map (``projects._BRIEF_DOOR_MODELS``); it is its
own module and does not touch the ``ProjectCreate`` path.

``populate_by_name=True`` lets ``target_url`` be supplied as either ``url`` (the
author-friendly alias) or ``target_url``. ``extra='allow'`` round-trips any
forward key untouched.

VideoSourceResponse.title: VideoSourceResponse
VideoSourceResponse.description:
One registered source clip.

``original_url`` is a presigned GET for the stored original (``None`` on a
backend that cannot presign). ``preview_status`` is always ``pending`` on
create — the derivative pass flips it to ``ready``/``failed`` later, and the
FE renders a placeholder until then.

VideoUploadCreateRequest.title: VideoUploadCreateRequest
VideoUploadCreateRequest.description:
What the client knows before it sends a single byte.

``bytes`` is the file's REAL size as the browser reports it, and it is used
for three things: refusing an upload that could never fit under the cap
(before anything is transferred), telling the client how many parts to slice,
and — at ``complete`` — proving that what arrived is the whole file.

⚠ That third use makes this field LOAD-BEARING, and it did not used to be.
This docstring previously said "a declaration, not a promise — ``complete``
composes what actually arrived rather than what was announced here", and that
was precisely the hole: a client that sent 4 of 16 parts and called
``complete`` got a 128 MiB fragment registered as a perfectly successful
``VideoSource``. ffprobe on a truncated MP4 returns ``{}`` (the ``moov`` atom
is at the end), ``footage_probe`` re-probes nothing, and the clip carries a
zeroed duration forever with nothing anywhere flagging it. ``complete`` now
requires parts ``1..part_count`` AND ``sum(parts) == bytes`` — see its
docstring for why the sum check is worth the coupling.

VideoUploadCreateResponse.title: VideoUploadCreateResponse
VideoUploadCreateResponse.description:
The plan the client executes.

``source_id`` is handed out HERE, before any byte moves, so the final object
key is fixed at create time. That is what makes the part keys and the final
key derivable by both sides without a second round trip, and what makes
``complete`` idempotent: the winner's row already has the id the loser would
have had to invent.

``expires_at`` is advisory — see ``_UPLOAD_TTL``.

VideoUploadPartResponse.title: VideoUploadPartResponse
VideoUploadPartResponse.description:
Acknowledgement of one stored part, plus the running state of the whole.

The running totals are returned on every part so a client that lost track
(tab reload, retried part, parallel PUTs finishing out of order) can resume
without a separate status call.

VisualType.title: VisualType
VisualType.description: Media provenance of a panel's picture (Appendix B).

BearerAuth.description: License token. Transport: `X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <token>` (not the Authorization header — that is reserved for caller-side auth).
